facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2025 planned-deployments report on 8 May 2025.
The report uses communications-provider plans as of January 2025.
The plans cover a horizon of up to three years.
The report includes private and publicly supported operator plans.
If all plans were realised, full fibre could reach 28.8 million homes by January 2028.
All-plan full-fibre coverage could reach 95%.
Gigabit-capable coverage could reach 97%.
High-confidence full-fibre plans could reach 86% by January 2028.
Rural gigabit-capable coverage could rise from 58% to 89%.
Around 1,100 additional FWA masts were planned or due for upgrade.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the infrastructure-reports collection on 19 December 2023.
The English collection was last updated on 19 November 2025.
The collection focuses on fixed and mobile network coverage and performance.
Connected Nations is described as an annual report.
Ofcom states it publishes two Connected Nations updates each year.
One update provides a mid-year coverage snapshot.
Another update reports planned network deployment.
Connected Nations 2025 is listed in the collection.
Planned Network Deployments 2025 is listed.
Older reports are routed to the National Archives.

facts.detail: BDUK published the annual QMI on 11 June 2026.
The QMI documents data strengths, limitations and production methods.
The reference area is the United Kingdom.
The data covers April 2012 to March 2026.
The release includes quarterly time series for 2024/25 and 2025/26 for the first time.
Superfast delivery was revised upward by about 730 premises.
Voucher delivery was revised upward by about 310 premises.
GIS delivery was revised downward by about 30 premises.
BDUK uses premises- and postcode-level source data in producing the statistics.
The QMI records a time lag caused by supplier data receipt and statistical production.

facts.detail: BDUK published the quarterly QMI on 19 February 2026.
The QMI documents strengths, limitations and methods.
Geographic lookups include ONS, NISRA, Scottish Government and AddressBase Premium data.
BDUK uses the most recent Connected Nations premises and postcode data available.
BDUK validates UPRNs returned by suppliers.
A 5% attrition rate is applied to expected-premises-passed data.
At the release date, 69% of voucher premises used the direct expected-premises methodology.
The remaining 31% were estimated using a multiplier approach.
The post-2022/23 voucher multiplier was 1.7.
GIS premises are excluded where another supplier built first.

facts.detail: The report documents quality characteristics and production methods.
A correction removed 140 hubs funded by other public bodies.
Reported 2024/25 hubs were revised from 380 to 240.
Geographic source data includes ONS, NISRA, Scottish Government and AddressBase Premium.
BDUK uses Ofcom premises- and postcode-level data.
The data covers delivery through 30 September 2025.
GIS suppliers submit monthly Stage 2 progress spreadsheets.
Only submissions passing BDUK quality checks are used.
The QMI warns that reporting can lag build completion by up to six months.
BDUK statistics are not directly comparable with Ofcom because premises bases differ.
